headline: Commission sets interview plan for new department director

meeting.voteItem: Motion to go into executive session
meeting.summary: The Civil Service Commission set interviews for the 30th and voted to invite DPS employees to take part in the selection process.
meeting.recap: The Civil Service Commission met in person and online through Microsoft Teams.[[0:00:30]] The goal was to finalize the timeline and selection process for the department's new leader.[[0:03:10]] A draft schedule sets interviews at 10:00, 12:00 and 2:00.[[0:05:00]] Commissioners agreed to keep the schedule as prepared and stay flexible.[[0:07:09]] Candidates will be told their interview times may be earlier or later, depending on public testimony.[[0:09:50]] The commission voted to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[0:12:35]] Interviews are set for the 30th.[[0:13:59]] All applicants will arrive at 9:00, be kept in a separate room, and be interviewed one at a time.[[0:15:06]] Each applicant will give a 3- to 5-minute summary of their statement before answering questions.[[0:15:20]] Employees are invited to watch the interviews live and send anonymous comments afterward.[[0:16:23]] The commission approved a motion to invite DPS employees to take part in the selection process.[[0:17:26]] A commissioner said an earlier call to keep DPS staff out applied only to an earlier stage.[[0:19:00]] The next meeting, on October 7, will have no hearing.[[0:21:33]] A long-postponed training was added to the November meeting agenda.[[0:22:13]] Commissioners divided five interview questions among themselves.[[0:24:24]] The meeting was adjourned.[[0:26:05]]
decided: The commission voted to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion).
The motion to invite DPS employees to take part in the selection process carried.
The commission voted to adjourn the meeting.
meeting.next: Yukari will draft the invitation email to DPS employees. A final email will tell candidates their interview time may be earlier or later depending on public testimony. The October 7 meeting will include a vote on a decision being sent to the commission and a check for new appeals. Final choices on who asks which question must be made after the meeting starts at 9:00.
